sources.title: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: Chapter 'Chemical Reactions and Equations': sections on chemical equations and balanced chemical equations (law of conservation of mass)

nodes.statement: Balance a chemical equation by changing coefficients so that each element has the same number of atoms on both sides.
Hydrogen burns in oxygen to form water. In formula form the unbalanced reaction is H2 + O2 -> H2O.
In H2 + O2 -> H2O the left side has 2 oxygen atoms and the right side has 1, so the oxygen count does not match. Hydrogen is 2 on each side.
Atoms are never created or destroyed in a chemical reaction (law of conservation of mass), so each element must have the same atom count on both sides of a balanced equation.
To balance an equation only the coefficients (the whole numbers in front of formulas) are changed. The subscripts inside a formula are fixed for that substance.
2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O has 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms on each side.
A subscript fixes the substance. H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide, a different compound from water, H2O.
For H2 + O2 -> H2O2 the hydrogen and oxygen counts match on both sides, yet the product is a different substance from water.
Fix the atom count by writing H2O2 for water, that is, by changing a subscript.
nodes.why_wrong: Changing a subscript changes the substance: H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide, not water. Only coefficients may change.

nodes.statement: Each atom is drawn as one equal circle, coloured by element, so the atom counts can be seen and checked.
nodes.what_is_lost: Atomic size, electrons, bonds and three-dimensional shape are not shown. Only the atom counts are exact.

steps: Count atoms. Left: H 2, O 2. Right: H 2, O 1. Oxygen is short on the right.
Change coefficients only: put 2 in front of H2 and 2 in front of H2O.
Recount. Left: H 4, O 2. Right: H 4, O 2. Balanced: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.

nodes.stem: Count the oxygen atoms on each side of H2 + O2 -> H2O. Which side is short?
nodes.answer: The right side. It has 1 oxygen atom against 2 on the left.
